name: Dennis Koshta
shortBio: I build AI systems, research model behavior, and make the evidence behind a result easier to inspect.
aboutParagraphs: My work covers language-model experiments, formal proofs, developer tools, and interactive software. I’m particularly interested in how we evaluate AI systems and where those evaluations fall short.
I work with proof checkers, evaluation tasks, and training experiments to understand what a system can do. I also study how model behavior changes when those checks become the training objective.
At Bronco AI, I work on evaluation systems for autonomous agents. The projects on this site are independent work, open-source contributions, and earlier team research.

I studied at the University of California, Santa Cruz, where my activities included NeuroTechSC and the Artificial Intelligence Explainability & Accountability Lab. At NeuroTechSC I led the Machine Learning and Data team, connecting signal processing, model training, and live application work.

collaborationParagraphs: I use Codex and Claude Code for implementation, experiments, and review. I set the direction, check the outputs, and decide what to keep. Each project page explains my contribution and credits collaborators and upstream work.

The Studio projects are collaborations with GPT and Claude. I direct the work, test the software, and iterate on the design. Research pages include methods, results, and limitations so you can judge the work for yourself.
